edition.name: Migne PL 3 (1844), Epistola Firmiliani ad Cyprianum, via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Quid ergo, inquiunt, fiet de his qui ab haereticis venientes sine Ecclesiae baptismo admissi sunt? Si de saeculo excesserunt, in eorum numero habentur qui apud nos catechisati quidem sunt, sed prius quam baptizarentur obierunt, non modo dicunt emolumentum veritatis et fidei, ad quam, relicto errore, pervenerant, etsi consummationem gratiae consecuti non sunt, morte praeventi. Qui autem adhuc in saeculo permanent baptizentur Ecclesiae Baptismo, ut remissionem peccatorum consequi possint, ne, per alienam praesumptionem, in pristino errore manentes, sine gratiae consummatione moriantur. Caeterum quale delictum est, vel illorum qui admittunt, vel eorum qui admittuntur, ut non ablutis per Ecclesiae lavacrum sordibus, nec peccatis expositis, usurpata temere communicatione contingant corpus et sanguinem Domini, cum scriptum sit: Quicumque ederit panem aut biberit calicem Domini indigne, reus erit corporis et sanguinis Domini.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore, they say, will happen to those who coming from heretics were admitted without Church baptism? If they have passed away from the world, they are considered among those who among us were catechized indeed, but before they were baptized died, not only do they say the advantage of truth and faith, to which, having left error, they arrived, even if they did not attain the completion of grace, having been prevented by death. Those who still remain in the world should be baptized with the Church's Baptism, so that they may be able to attain the remission of sins, lest, through another's presumption, remaining in their former error, they die without the completion of grace. Moreover, what kind of fault is it, either of those who admit or of those who are admitted, that without the stains being washed away through the Church's bath, nor sins being exposed, they touch the body and blood of the Lord with a communication usurped rashly, when it is written: Whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily, will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

choices.why: indicating the origin of the individuals
specifying the type of baptism they lacked
describing the manner in which they received communion

bible_refs.note: Quicumque ederit panem aut biberit calicem Domini indigne, reus erit corporis et sanguinis Domini

pass_b_english: Someone may ask, "What will become of those who were admitted without the Church's baptism after coming from heretics?" If they have already died, we count them among those who were catechized here but passed away before receiving baptism. They not only gained the benefit of the truth and faith they reached after abandoning their error, even though death prevented them from receiving the full completion of grace. As for those who are still alive, they must be baptized with the Church's baptism so that they may obtain the forgiveness of sins. Otherwise, relying on someone else's presumption, they would remain in their former error and die without the completion of grace. Besides, what fault lies either with those who admit them or with those who are admitted, that without having their stains washed away in the Church's bath and without having their sins laid bare, they dare to touch the body and blood of the Lord by rashly claiming a share in the communion? For it is written: "Whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord" (1 Corinthians 11:27).
